
## §5.1.1: The *Hypersyntrix* ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}$) & Multi-Scale Encapsulation {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">MULTI-SCALE TRANSCENDENCE &amp; STRATUM D (SM, PP. 80–84, EQS. 20, 20a, 20b)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Crossing the Scale Threshold: *Hyperkategorien*
* Chapters 1–4 traced base-level Syntrices ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 0}{\mathbf{M}} \equiv \mathbf{y}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}$), yet nature and cognition are **irreducibly multi-scale**: an entire network of lower-level systems becomes a single elementary building block at the next scale of organization.
* In §5.1 (SM, pp. 81–84), Heim defines the **Metroplex ersten Grades**—the **Hypersyntrix ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}$)** (which he calls a *Hyperkategorie*):
$$
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \;\equiv\; \big\langle\langle \underline{\mathrm{F}},\, \widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \rangle \underline{\mathrm{r}} \big\rangle \quad \lor \quad \widetilde{\mathrm{a}}| \;\equiv\; (\widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_i)_N \tag{SM-20}
$$

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**The Higher-Order Triad & Corporate Pairings (SM Eqs. 20a, 20b):**
1. **Hypermetrophor (${}^1\mathbf{w}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}} \equiv (\mathbf{y}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}_i)_N$):** Encapsulates $N$ complete base Syntrices from $T0$ as 0-dimensional objects.
2. **Metroplexsynkolator (${}^1\mathfrak{f} \equiv S(2)$):** Second-order Syntrixfunktor of valency $r$ correlating entire Syntrixfelder into higher-order syndromes, terminating at the **Nullmetroplex 1. Ordnung (${}^1\mathbf{M}_0$)**.
3. **Concentric (SM-20a) & Excentric (SM-20b) Pairings:**
$$
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} K_s & C_s \\ K_m & C_m \end{smallmatrix} \right\} \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{b}},\; \overline{|B|},\; \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{c}} \;\;\text{(SM-20a)}, \quad
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}}^{(l)} \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} K_s & C_s \\ K_m & C_m \end{smallmatrix} \right\}^{(m)} \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{b}},\; \overline{||},\; \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{c}} \;\;\text{(SM-20b)}
$$
Higher-order *Metroplexkorporatoren* inherit *Spaltbarkeit* (splittability) and the 4 elementary selection structures.
:::

## §5.1.2–5.1.3: *Hypertotalitäten*, Higher *Metroplexe* ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}$) & *Duale Tektonik* {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: METROPLEXTOTALITÄT (T₁..Tₙ), FUNCTOR HIERARCHY S(n+1) &amp; SM EQS. 21–24</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Metroplextotalität ($T_1$), *Protosimplexe* & Functor Hierarchy $S(n+1)$ (SM, pp. 85–88):**
* **Syntrixtotalität ($T0$)** vs. **Metroplextotalität 1. Grades ($T_1$):** $T_1$ is the totality of all realizations of Hypersyntrices and their corporate combinations (*Hypertotalitäten* & *Enyphanmetroplexe*).
* **Generative Functor Hierarchy:**
  * $S1 \equiv \mathfrak{f}$: Generates grade-0 Syntrices ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 0}{\mathbf{M}}$) from $\mathbf{AP}_0$.
  * $S2 \equiv {}^1\mathfrak{f}$: Generates grade-1 Hypersyntrices ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}$) from $\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 0}{\mathbf{M}}$.
  * $S(n+1) \equiv {}^n\mathfrak{f}$: Generates grade-$n$ Metroplexe ($\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}$) from grade-$(n-1)$ Metroplexe.
* **Protosimplexe (SM, p. 87):** Minimal, irreducible structural units within a state totality $T_n$ serving as unanalyzable atomic objects at the next level.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Recursive Grade-$n$ Hierarchy & Elementary Basis (SM Eqs. 21–24, pp. 89–92):**
$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \equiv \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 0}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \;\;(\text{SM-21}), \qquad
\widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_i \equiv \widetilde{\mathrm{p}}_{(k)i} \;\;(\text{SM-22}), \qquad
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}},\; \overline{|B|},\; \mathrm{C},\; \overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{p}}_{(k)} \;\;(1 \le k \le 4,\;\text{SM-23})
$$
$$
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n+1}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \;\equiv\; \big\langle \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{F}},\, \overset{\scriptscriptstyle\sim}{\mathbf{M}}{}^n\widetilde{\mathrm{a}}\,\underline{\mathrm{r}} \big\rangle \quad \lor \quad \overset{\scriptscriptstyle\sim}{\mathbf{M}}{}^n\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \;\equiv\; \left(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_{(p)}\right)_{N_n} \tag{SM-24}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Duale Endogene Tektonik & *Kontraktion* (SM, p. 93):**
1. **Graduelle Tektonik (Vertical / Grade Tectonics):** The vertical, nested compositional hierarchy of the Metroplex across its associated lower grades $0 \le k \le n-1$.
2. **Syndromatische Tektonik (Horizontal / Syndrome Tectonics):** The horizontal, sequential organization of syndrome layers generated within a given grade by the active synkolators ${}^k\mathfrak{f}$.
3. **Kontraktion ($\kappa \colon \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}} \to \overset{\scriptscriptstyle m}{\mathbf{M}}',\; m < n$):** Formally compresses a high-grade Metroplex into an effective lower-grade representation while preserving dominant structural invariants.
:::

## §5.1.4–5.1.5: *Syntrokline Metroplexbrücken* & *Metroplexdiabatik* {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: SYNTROKLINE BRÜCKEN (SM EQS. 25, 25a), EN-KOMBINATION (SM-26) &amp; RÜCKKOPPELUNG</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Syntrokline Metroplexbrücken (SM Eqs. 25, 25a, pp. 94–98):**
Totalities $T_n$ act as *Etagen* (floors); bridges ${}^{n+N}\alpha$ act as *Aufzüge* (elevators) lifting lower-grade structures across $N$ intervening grades:
$$
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n+N}{\tilde{\alpha}} \;\equiv\; \underset{n}{\overset{n+N}{\mathrm{S}}}\, \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \Big[ \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n-1}{\widetilde{\Phi}}_{j(n)\gamma}\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n-1}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}_{j(n)\gamma}, \underline{\mathrm{m}}_{j(n)\gamma}\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}_\gamma, \underline{\mathrm{r}}_\gamma\big) \big(\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n+1}{\widetilde{\mathrm{f}}}, \mathrm{p}\big) \Big]_{\gamma=1}^{k_{(n)}} \tag{SM-25a}
$$
**Endogene Kombinationen (SM Eq. 26, p. 102):**
$$
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle\sim}{\mathbf{M}}{}^n \;\equiv\; \overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \,\mathrm{EN}\, \overset{\scriptscriptstyle p+q}{\mathbf{M}}\widetilde{\mathrm{b}} \qquad (p + q \le n \;\land\; q > 0) \tag{SM-26}
$$
:::

::: {.remark-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Remark (Conceptual Preamble: Why Higher Scale Hierarchies Require an $(\infty,1)$-Topos):**
Following Marquis (2009), Zalamea (2012), and Lurie (2009), when a system of Syntrices is bundled into a higher-grade Metroplex, corporate transformations become 1-morphisms, transformations between those become 2-morphisms, and so on *ad infinitum*. In strict 1-category theory, forcing multi-scale identifications to hold as rigid point-set equalities causes the hierarchy to collapse into inconsistency. In an **$(\infty,1)$-topos**, composition is governed by coherent higher homotopies rather than brittle strict equality.
:::

:::

## §5.2.1: Ambient $(\infty, 1)$-Topos $\Xsyn$ & Universe Stratification {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: META-THEORETIC JUSTIFICATION, DEF. 5.1 &amp; CUMULATIVE UNIVERSES (FIG. 5.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.scholium-box}
**Scholium (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Ambient $(\infty,1)$-Topos & Dendroidal Segal Objects):**
Why formulate the Metroplex hierarchy inside a single ambient $(\infty, 1)$-topos $\Xsyn = \mathbf{Sh}_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn)$ rather than iterating sites $\mathbf{Site}_{n+1} = \mathbf{Sh}(\mathbf{Site}_n)$?
1. **Universe Safety ($\mathcal{U}_0 \in \mathcal{U}_1 \in \mathcal{U}_2$):** Iterated site-building explodes set-theoretic universes at every step. Housing all grades inside a single $\mathcal{U}_0$-presentable $(\infty,1)$-topos ensures every Metroplex $\mathbf{M}^n$ remains $\mathcal{U}_0$-small inside $\Xsyn$.
2. **Dendroidal Complete Segal Objects ($\dCSeg(\Xsyn)$):** Because synkolators $f \in \Osyn(m)$ have multi-ary valence $m \ge 1$, grade-1 Hypersyntrices are modeled over the Moerdijk–Weiss tree category $\mathbf{\Omega}$, avoiding strict associativity pitfalls via Rezk's completeness condition.
3. **Adjoint Syntroclinic Bridges:** Change-of-operad adjunctions $(\phi_{n, n+N})_! \dashv (\phi_{n, n+N})^*$ replace ad-hoc cross-scale mappings.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 5.1: Ambient $(\infty, 1)$-Topos $\Xsyn$ & Postnikov Tower**
Fix Grothendieck universes $\mathcal{U}_0 \in \mathcal{U}_1 \in \mathcal{U}_2$ and $\mathcal{S} \coloneqq \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_0}$. The **Ambient Syntrometric $(\infty, 1)$-Topos** is the left-exact topological localization:
$$
\Xsyn \;\coloneqq\; \mathbf{Sh}_\infty\big(\Ctx, \Jsyn\big) \;\coloneqq\; L_{\Jsyn}\!\Big(\operatorname{Fun}\big((\Ctx)^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathcal{S}\big)\Big)
$$
1. **0-Truncated Recovery:** $\tau_{\le 0}\Xsyn \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\Ctx, \Jsyn) = \Esyn$ recovers the 1-topos of Chapter 1.
2. **Higher Homotopy Truncation:** $\tau_{\le m} \colon \Xsyn \to \Xsyn^{\le m}$ is left adjoint to the inclusion $\iota_m \colon \Xsyn^{\le m} \hookrightarrow \Xsyn$.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.claim-ceiling .fragment .glow-pulse}
**Size Discipline & Cumulative Universe Stratification (Fig. 5.2):**
* **$\mathcal{U}_0$ (Internal):** Small site $\Ctx$, objects $X \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Xsyn)$, internal Metroplexe $\mathbf{M}^n \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Met_n(\Xsyn))$.
* **$\mathcal{U}_1$ (Ambient):** Space $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_0}$, topos $\Xsyn$, categories $\Met_n(\Xsyn)$ and $\Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)$ ($\mathcal{U}_0$-presentable, locally $\mathcal{U}_0$-small).
* **$\mathcal{U}_2$ (Meta-Slice):** External functor categories $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}, \Met_n(\Xsyn))$, external slice totalities $T_n^{\mathrm{ext}}$, or enlarged $\Xsyn^{(k)} \coloneqq \mathbf{Sh}_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn; \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{U}_k})$.
:::

## §5.2.2–5.2.3: Dendroidal Complete Segal Spaces & Grafting Proof {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: DENDROIDAL SEGAL SPACES (DEF. 5.2), GRAFTING PROOF (PROP. 5.3) &amp; OPERAD AXIOM (ASSUMP. 5.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 5.2: Dendroidal Complete Segal Objects $\dCSeg(\Xsyn)$**
Let $\mathbf{\Omega}$ be the Moerdijk–Weiss dendroidal category of finite rooted trees ($i \colon \mathbf{\Delta} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{\Omega}$ embedding linear trees $[k]$). A dendroidal object $X \colon \mathbf{\Omega}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \Xsyn$ is a **Dendroidal Complete Segal Space** ($X \in \dCSeg(\Xsyn)$) if:
1. **Dendroidal Segal Condition:** For every tree $T \in \mathbf{\Omega}$ with vertices $V(T)$ and $n(v)$-corollas $C_{n(v)} \hookrightarrow T$ glued along inner edges $E_{\mathrm{int}}(T)$:
$$
X(T) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \lim_{v \in V(T)}^{\Xsyn} X(C_{n(v)}) \;\simeq\; X(C_{n(v_1)}) \mathop{\times}\limits^{\mathrm{h}}_{X(\eta_{e_1})} \cdots \mathop{\times}\limits^{\mathrm{h}}_{X(\eta_{e_k})} X(C_{n(v_{k+1})})
$$
2. **Rezk Completeness:** $(i^*X)_0 \xrightarrow{\sim} (i^*X)_{\mathrm{hoequiv}} \subset (i^*X)_1$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proposition 5.3 & Proof (Explicit Dendroidal Segal Grafting for Binary Hypersyntrices):**
Let $T = C_2^{(v)} \circ_e C_2^{(u)} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{\Omega})$ graft two binary 2-corollas along inner edge $\eta_e$.
1. **Grafting Pullback:** The dendroidal spine is the pushout $\operatorname{Sc}[T] = C_2^{(v)} \amalg_{\eta_e} C_2^{(u)}$ in $\mathbf{\Omega}$, mapping to the homotopy pullback $X(T) \xrightarrow{\sim} X(C_2^{(v)}) \times_{X(\eta_e)}^{\mathrm{h}} X(C_2^{(u)})$ in $\Xsyn$.
2. **Ternary Composite $\partial_{\eta_e}^* \colon X(T) \to X(C_3)$:** Contracting $\eta_e$ gives the inner face $\partial_{\eta_e} \colon C_3 \hookrightarrow T$. Inverting the Segal equivalence up to homotopy and applying $\partial_{\eta_e}^*$ composes compatible binary operations $(v, u) \mapsto v \circ_e u \in X(C_3)$.
3. **Associativity Homotopy:** On a 3-vertex tree $T_3$ with inner edges $e_1, e_2$, commuting face maps $\partial_{e_1}\partial_{e_2} = \partial_{e_2}\partial_{e_1} \colon C_4 \hookrightarrow T_3$ induce $(w \circ_1 v) \circ_1 u \simeq w \circ_1 (v \circ_2 u)$ inside $X(C_4)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

<div class="interactive-panel">
  <h4>Interactive Dendroidal Corolla Grafting &amp; Segal Spine Explorer (Prop. 5.3)</h4>
  <p class="widget-context-note">
  <b>Context (§5.2.2, Prop. 5.3):</b> Step through the dendroidal Segal condition on the grafted binary tree $T = C_2^{(v)} \circ_e C_2^{(u)}$, the inner-edge contraction $\partial_{\eta_e}$ yielding the composite ternary corolla $C_3$, and the 3-vertex associativity homotopy.
  </p>

</div>

::: {.thm-box .fragment .zoom-in}
**Assumption 5.4: The Metroplex Operadic Realization Axiom ($\{\On\}_{n \ge 0}$)**
There exists an inductive family of internal $(\infty, 1)$-operads $\{\On\}_{n \ge 0}$ in $\Xsyn$ ($\mathcal{O}_0 \coloneqq N_\Delta(\Osyn)$) with:
1. **Free-Forgetful Monad Adjunction:** $\Free_{\On} \colon \Xsyn \rightleftarrows \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \colon U_n$ ($T_{\On} = U_n \circ \Free_{\On}$).
2. **Change-of-Operad Adjunctions:** Operad morphisms $\phi_{n, n+1} \colon \On \to \mathcal{O}_{n+1}$ induce $(\phi_{n, n+1})_! \colon \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \rightleftarrows \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+1}}(\Xsyn) \colon (\phi_{n, n+1})^*$, with $\phi_{n, n+N} \coloneqq \phi_{n+N-1, n+N} \circ \dots \circ \phi_{n, n+1}$.
:::

## §5.3.1: Uniform Metroplex Categories $\Met_n(\Xsyn)$ & Toy Example {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: UNIFORM METROPLEX CATEGORIES (DEFS. 5.5–5.6), TOY EXAMPLE &amp; 3D TRANSCENDENCE TOWER (FIG. 5.1)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 5.5: Uniform Categories of Grade-$n$ Metroplexe $\Met_n(\Xsyn)$**
For every grade $n \ge 0$, $\Met_n(\Xsyn)$ is a full $(\infty, 1)$-subcategory of $\Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)$:
1. **Grade $n = 0$ (Base Syntrices):** $\Met_0(\Xsyn) \coloneqq \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_0}(\Xsyn)$.
2. **Grade $n = 1$ (Hypersyntrices):** $\Met_1(\Xsyn) \simeq \dCSeg(\Xsyn) \hookrightarrow \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_1}(\Xsyn)$ (with linear spine $i^*\Met_1(\Xsyn) = \CSeg(\Xsyn) \simeq \operatorname{Cat}_\infty(\Xsyn)$).
3. **Grade $n \ge 2$ (Higher Metroplexe):** $\Met_n(\Xsyn) \subseteq \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn)$ generated by hypermetrophoric colimits of grade-$(n-1)$ diagrams.
Equipped with conservative forgetful functors $U_n^{\Met} \colon \Met_n(\Xsyn) \to \Xsyn$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 5.6: Hypermetrophors as Simplicial Diagrams $H_n$**
For $n \ge 1$, a **Grade-$n$ Hypermetrophor** is a simplicial diagram $H_n \colon \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \Met_{n-1}(\Xsyn)$ whose vertices $[0] \mapsto H_{n,0}$ are grade-$(n-1)$ Metroplexe and whose 1-simplices $[1] \mapsto H_{n,1}$ encode corporate pairings ($\mathbf{Kor}_n$). Its geometric realization colimit is:
$$
\HypMet_n \;\coloneqq\; \colim_{[k] \in \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} \big( U_{n-1}^{\Met} \circ H_n([k]) \big) \;\in\; \Xsyn, \qquad
\overset{\scriptscriptstyle n}{\mathbf{M}}\mathcal{S} \;\coloneqq\; \Free_{\On}(\HypMet_n)
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.remark-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Remark (Toy Example: The Hypersyntrix $\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}}$ as an Internal 2-Object Category):**
Consider two base Syntrices $\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2 \in \Met_0(\Xsyn)$ coupled by a corporate pairing $\mathbf{Kor}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2)$. How do they form a grade-1 Hypersyntrix $\overset{\scriptscriptstyle 1}{\mathbf{M}} \in \CSeg(\Xsyn)$?
* **Object Space ($[0]$):** $C_0 \coloneqq \mathcal{S}_1 \sqcup \mathcal{S}_2$ (the Hypermetrophor ${}^1\mathbf{w}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}$). Every entire lower-level Syntrix becomes a single *point* (0-simplex) at grade 1!
* **Morphism Space ($[1]$):** $C_1 \coloneqq \mathbf{Kor}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2) \sqcup \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{S}_1} \sqcup \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{S}_2}$ (the Metroplexsynkolator ${}^1\mathfrak{f}$).
* **Segal Composition ($[2]$):** $C_2 \cong C_1 \times_{C_0} C_1$, ensuring sequential corporate couplings compose associatively up to coherent homotopy.
:::

## §5.3.2–5.3.3: Syntroclinic Bridge Proof & Postnikov Contraction $\tau_{\le m}$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: BRIDGE LIFTING PROOF (DEF. 5.7, PROP. 5.8, FIG. 5.3) &amp; POSTNIKOV CONTRACTION (DEF. 5.9, PROP. 5.10, FIG. 5.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 5.7 & Proposition 5.8: Syntroclinic Bridge Adjunction**
For grades $n \ge 0$ and $N \ge 1$, the **Syntroclinic Bridge** is the left adjoint extension-of-scalars functor:
$$
B_{n, n+N} \;\coloneqq\; (\phi_{n, n+N})_! \colon \Alg_{\On}(\Xsyn) \;\rightleftarrows\; \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+N}}(\Xsyn) \;\colon (\phi_{n, n+N})^* =: R_{n+N, n}
$$
On the subcategory $\mathcal{I}_n \subseteq \Met_n(\Xsyn)$ of invariant syndromes, the restricted bridge $B_{n, n+N}|_{\mathcal{I}_n}$ is **fully faithful** if and only if for every $X \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathcal{I}_n)$, the adjunction unit is an equivalence in $\Met_n(\Xsyn)$:
$$
\eta_X \colon X \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; R_{n+N, n}\big(B_{n, n+N}(X)\big)
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Proposition 5.8 (Standard Adjunction Criterion for Fully Faithful Lifting):**
For any $X, Y \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathcal{I}_n)$, the adjunction $B_{n, n+N} \dashv R_{n+N, n}$ provides a natural homotopy equivalence of mapping spaces:
$$
\Map_{\Alg_{\mathcal{O}_{n+N}}}\!\big(B_{n, n+N}(X),\, B_{n, n+N}(Y)\big) \;\simeq\; \Map_{\Alg_{\On}}\!\big(X,\, R_{n+N, n}(B_{n, n+N}(Y))\big)
$$
Under this equivalence, the action of $B_{n, n+N}$ on mapping spaces $\Map(X, Y) \to \Map(B(X), B(Y))$ factors as post-composition with the unit morphism $(\eta_Y)_* \colon \Map(X, Y) \to \Map(X, R(B(Y)))$. By the Yoneda Lemma in $(\infty, 1)$-categories (Lurie 2009, §5.1.3), $(\eta_Y)_*$ is a homotopy equivalence for all $X \in \mathcal{I}_n$ iff $\eta_Y \colon Y \xrightarrow{\sim} R_{n+N, n}(B_{n, n+N}(Y))$ is an equivalence. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 5.11: Bisimplicial Tectonic Object $\Tect(\mathcal{S})$**
For an associative Metroplex $\mathcal{S} \in \Met_n(\Xsyn)$, its dual endogenous architecture is realized as a bisimplicial object:
$$
\Tect(\mathcal{S}) \;\in\; \operatorname{Fun}\big(\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \times \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}},\; \Xsyn\big)
$$
with commuting vertical face/degeneracy operators ($d_i^v, s_i^v$ on $\operatorname{Gr}_\bullet$, grades $0 \le k \le n-1$) and horizontal operators ($d_j^h, s_j^h$ on $\operatorname{Syn}_\bullet$, syndrome layers).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Definition 5.12: Homological Banach Realization Functor $\RBan$**
On $\Xsyn^{\mathrm{coord}} \subseteq \Xsyn$ (sheaves $X$ with finitely generated total homology of $\Gamma(X)$ and basis $B_X$), via free $\mathbb{R}$-linearization $\mathbb{R}[-] \colon \mathcal{S} \to s\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}}$ and Dold–Kan normalization $N_\bullet \colon s\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbf{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})$:
$$
\RBan(X) \;\coloneqq\; \bigoplus_{k=0}^\infty H_k\!\Big( N_\bullet\big(\mathbb{R}[\Gamma(X)]\big) \Big)_{\ell^1} \;\in\; \operatorname{Obj}(\FinBan)
$$
Degree $k=0$ recovers $H_0 \cong \mathbb{R}[\pi_0(\Gamma(X))]$, while $k \ge 1$ preserves higher homotopical invariants, yielding $\Tect_{\mathbf{Ban}}(\mathcal{S}) \coloneqq \RBan \circ \Tect(\mathcal{S})$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .zoom-in}
**Theorem 5.13: Tectonic 2-Fold Segal Realization Theorem**
Pre-composing with $\operatorname{diag} \colon \mathbf{\Delta} \to \mathbf{\Delta} \times \mathbf{\Delta}$ ($[k] \mapsto \Tect(\mathcal{S})_{k,k}$) yields the **Total Tectonic Object**:
$$
\big|\Tect(\mathcal{S})\big|_{\mathbf{\Delta}} \;\coloneqq\; \colim_{\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}}\big(\operatorname{diag}^* \Tect(\mathcal{S})\big) \;\simeq\; \colim_{\mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \times \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} \Tect(\mathcal{S})_{p,q}
$$
unifying vertical gradual and horizontal syndromatic architectures into a single coherent homotopy type in $\Xsyn$.
:::

:::

Applies Dold–Kan normalization in both simplicial directions of $\Tect_{\mathbf{Ban}}(\mathcal{S}) \colon \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \times \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \FinBan$ to produce a first-quadrant bicomplex $(C_{p,q}(\mathcal{S}), \partial^{\mathrm{grad}}, \partial^{\mathrm{syn}})$.

::: {#coh-pane-2 .syn-tab-pane}
**2. Lawvere–Schreiber Cohesive Quadruple (Def. 5.14)**
Global sections $\Gamma \colon \Xsyn \to \mathcal{S}$ extends to an adjoint quadruple where $\Disc$ preserves finite products and $\Pi(X \times Y) \simeq \Pi(X) \times \Pi(Y)$:
$$
\Pi \;\dashv\; \Disc \;\dashv\; \Gamma \;\dashv\; \Codisc \qquad \left(\Xsyn \underset{\Disc,\, \Codisc}{\overset{\Pi,\, \Gamma}{\rightleftarrows}} \mathcal{S}\right)
$$
:::

::: {#coh-pane-3 .syn-tab-pane}
**3. Shape Modality $\int \coloneqq \Disc \circ \Pi$ (Smooth *Äondyne*)**
For any Metroplex $\mathcal{S} \in \Xsyn$, $\int(\mathcal{S})$ extracts its **smooth path-homotopy type** (*Äondyne*).
:::

::: {#coh-pane-4 .syn-tab-pane}
**4. Flat ($\flat \coloneqq \Disc \circ \Gamma$) & Sharp ($\sharp \coloneqq \Codisc \circ \Gamma$) Modalities**
$\int \dashv \flat \dashv \sharp \colon \Xsyn \to \Xsyn$. Here $\flat(\mathcal{S})$ extracts the **underlying discrete combinatorial skeleton** (*Diskreter Enyphanmetroplex*), while $\sharp(\mathcal{S})$ embeds into the codiscrete envelope.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 5.15 (Eilenberg–Zilber & Spectral Convergence):**
By the Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier Theorem, $N_\bullet(\operatorname{diag}^*\Tect_{\mathbf{Ban}}(\mathcal{S})) \simeq \operatorname{Tot}(C_{\bullet,\bullet}(\mathcal{S}))$ with $D = \partial^{\mathrm{grad}} + (-1)^p \partial^{\mathrm{syn}}$. Since $C_{p,q} = 0$ for $p < 0$ or $q < 0$, the column filtration $F_p\operatorname{Tot}_m = \bigoplus_{i \le p} C_{i, m-i}$ is bounded below and exhaustive, guaranteeing finite-stage convergence $E^\infty_{p,q} \cong \operatorname{Gr}_p H_{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot})$ (Mac Lane 1998). A non-vanishing differential $d^r \ne 0$ ($r \ge 2$) is the exact homological obstruction to lifting a gradual $p$-cycle across $r$ vertical grades without modifying syndrome level by $r-1$ (**Metroplexdiabatik**, SM p. 103). $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Carnap 5.1 (Scale-Relativity & Resolving Kim's Downward Causation):**
Within Ontic Structural Realism (Ladyman & Ross 2007; French 2014), Theorem 5.15 and $(\phi_{n,n+N})_! \dashv (\phi_{n,n+N})^*$ dissolve Jaegwon Kim's causal exclusion paradox: macro-scale constraint is not an anomalous force violating grade-$0$ dynamics, but the transgression differential $d^r$ and right-adjoint restriction $(\phi_{n,n+N})^*$ selecting globally compatible cohomology classes in $\operatorname{Tot}(C_{\bullet,\bullet})$.
:::

## §5.3.6–5.3.7: Slice Totality $T_n$, *Protosimplexe* & $EN$-Operator {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: SLICE TOTALITIES (DEF. 5.16), PROTOSIMPLEXE (DEF. 5.17) &amp; EN-OPERATOR (DEF. 5.18)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 5.16: State Totality & Grade-$n$ Slice Category $T_n$**
For a generative blueprint object $G_n \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Met_n(\Xsyn))$, the structured realization category of grade-$n$ state totality $\mathsf{Tot}_n$ is the slice category:
$$
T_n \;\coloneqq\; \Met_n(\Xsyn) / G_n
$$
* **Terminal Object:** $\operatorname{id}_{G_n} \colon G_n \to G_n$.
* **Initial Object (*Nullmetroplex* ${}^n\mathbf{M}_0$):** $(0_n \to G_n)$ modeling structural exhaustion.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 5.17: Augmented Subobject-Minimal Protosimplex**
Let $\Alg_{\On}^0$ be the category of augmented algebras over the base constant subalgebra $\Free_{\On}(\emptyset)$. An object $\mathcal{P} \in \operatorname{Obj}(T_n)$ is a **Protosimplex of Grade $n$** if $\mathcal{P} \not\cong \Free_{\On}(\emptyset)$ and it has no proper non-trivial augmented sub-algebras:
$$
\forall A \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P} \text{ in } \Alg_{\On}^0, \qquad A \cong \Free_{\On}(\emptyset) \quad \lor \quad A \cong \mathcal{P}
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 5.18: Endogenous Synthesis ($\SynEN$) & Absorption ($\AbsEN$)**
$$
\SynEN_{p,q}^n \colon \Met_p(\Xsyn) \times \Met_q(\Xsyn) \longrightarrow \Met_n(\Xsyn) \qquad (p + q = n,\; q > 0)
$$
$$
\AbsEN_n^{p+q} \colon \Met_n(\Xsyn) \times \Met_{p+q}(\Xsyn) \longrightarrow \Met_n(\Xsyn) \qquad (p + q \le n,\; q > 0)
$$
Strict inequality $p + q \le n$ prevents infinite recursive runaway during combination.
:::

:::

| **Syndromatische Tektonik** | Horizontal simplicial axis $\operatorname{Syn}_\bullet$ of bisimplicial object | **C-Model** (Def. 5.11) |
| **Banach Realization ($\RBan$)** | Homological Dold–Kan composite $\bigoplus_k H_k(N_\bullet(\mathbb{R}[\Gamma(-)]))_{\ell^1}$ | **C-Model** (Def. 5.12) |
| **Endogene Kombination ($\operatorname{EN}$)** | Admissible operators $\SynEN_{p,q}^n, \AbsEN_n^{p+q}$ ($p+q \le n, q > 0$) | **A (Axiom)** (Def. 5.18) |
| **Nullmetroplex (${}^n\mathbf{M}_0$)** | Initial slice object $(0_n \to G_n)$ modeling structural exhaustion | **C-Model** (Def. 5.16) |
